title: Norm transition frames and tensor-power section gluing
statement:
Let $p:Y	o Z$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For each open $V\subseteq Z$ let $
u_V:\Gamma(p^{-1}V,\mathcal O_Y)	o\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$ preserve multiplication and $1$, and suppose these maps commute with restriction. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], $(V_i)_{i\in I}$ an open cover of $Z$, and $e_i$ a generating section of $M|_{p^{-1}V_i}$, meaning that $a\mapsto ae_i$ is an isomorphism from the structure sheaf to that restriction. Define the unique units $u_{ij}$ on $p^{-1}(V_i\cap V_j)$ by $e_i=u_{ij}e_j$, and set $v_{ij}=
u_{V_i\cap V_j}(u_{ij})$. Then $v_{ij}$ are units satisfying $v_{ii}=1$, $v_{ji}=v_{ij}^{-1}$ and $v_{ik}=v_{ij}v_{jk}$ on triple intersections. There exist an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module $N$ and generating sections $f_i$ on $V_i$ with $f_i=v_{ij}f_j$. For these fixed $N,f_i$, every integer $n\geq1$ and section $s\in\Gamma(Y,M^{\otimes n})$ determine a unique section $t\in\Gamma(Z,N^{\otimes n})$ with $$t|_{V_i}=
u_{V_i}(b_i)f_i^{\otimes n},\qquad s|_{p^{-1}V_i}=b_i e_i^{\otimes n}.$$ Here $M^{\otimes n},N^{\otimes n}$ are the tensor powers of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]; they are invertible, $e_i^{\otimes n},f_i^{\otimes n}$ are generators, and their transition functions are $u_{ij}^n,v_{ij}^n$, respectively. No finiteness, power identity, or vanishing hypothesis on $p,
u$ is imposed.

proof.text: On $p^{-1}(V_i\cap V_j)$ the inverse of the frame isomorphism $a\mapsto ae_j$ gives a unique coefficient $u_{ij}$ for $e_i$. Reversing the indices gives $e_j=u_{ji}e_i$, hence $u_{ij}u_{ji}=1$ by uniqueness of coefficients in the frame $e_i$. Thus these coefficients are units. On triple intersections substitute $e_j=u_{jk}e_k$ into $e_i=u_{ij}e_j$ and compare coefficients in $e_k$ to obtain $u_{ik}=u_{ij}u_{jk}$; the same uniqueness gives $u_{ii}=1$. All formulas use the restricted coefficients on the displayed intersection.

proof.text:
Apply $
u$ on each overlap. Multiplicativity and preservation of $1$ give $v_{ij}
u(u_{ji})=
u(1)=1$, so $v_{ij}$ is a unit and $v_{ji}=v_{ij}^{-1}$. They also give $v_{ii}=1$. Restriction compatibility lets us apply the triple-intersection map to the identity of step 1, obtaining $v_{ik}=v_{ij}v_{jk}$. These statements require neither additivity nor any power or vanishing axiom for $
u$.

source.place: Tag 0BCY, divisors-lemma-norm-invertible, proof: the v cocycle

proof.text: Use part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] on $Z$ with local modules $\mathcal O_{V_i}$ and $\varphi_{ij}$ multiplication by $v_{ij}$ from chart $i$ to chart $j$. These are module isomorphisms, and $\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}=\varphi_{ik}$ by step 2. Obtain $N$ and $\alpha_i:N|_{V_i}\simeq\mathcal O_{V_i}$ with $\alpha_j=v_{ij}\alpha_i$. Put $f_i=\alpha_i^{-1}(1)$. Then $\alpha_j(f_i)=v_{ij}$ and $\alpha_j(f_j)=1$, whence $f_i=v_{ij}f_j$. These sections are frames. On any affine neighbourhood $W\subseteq V_i$, $N|_W\simeq\mathcal O_W\simeq\widetilde{\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] with rank one; hence $N$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-def-coherent] and locally free of rank one, so invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module].

proof.text: For $M$ and $N$ separately, induct on $n\geq1$. Tensor products remain invertible by (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], applied with the identity morphism. For frames, the base $n=1$ is given. At $n+1$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-tensor-comparison] identifies the restricted tensor product with the tensor product of the restricted factors and respects pure sections. Tensor the frame isomorphisms from the induction hypothesis and the original frame, and precompose with the inverse of $\mathcal O\otimes\mathcal O\simeq\mathcal O$ from [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-symmetric-monoidal]. This gives the frame $e_i^{\otimes(n+1)}$ (respectively $f_i^{\otimes(n+1)}$). By bilinearity in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $(u_{ij}^{n}e_j^{\otimes n})\otimes(u_{ij}e_j)=u_{ij}^{n+1}e_j^{\otimes(n+1)}$, and likewise for $v$. This proves all tensor-power, generator and transition assertions.

Fix $n$ and $s$. The frame isomorphisms of step 4 give unique $b_i$ with $s=b_ie_i^{\otimes n}$ on $p^{-1}V_i$. On an overlap, equality of the restrictions of $s$ and $e_i^{\otimes n}=u_{ij}^ne_j^{\otimes n}$ imply $b_j=b_i u_{ij}^n$. Restriction compatibility and multiplicativity give $
u(b_j)=
u(b_i)v_{ij}^n$ (the power identity here follows by induction from multiplication, not from a degree axiom). Consequently $
u(b_i)f_i^{\otimes n}=
u(b_i)v_{ij}^nf_j^{\otimes n}=
u(b_j)f_j^{\otimes n}$ on $V_i\cap V_j$.

source.place: Tag 0BCZ, divisors-lemma-norm-map-invertible, proof: the local coefficient calculation, applied to a section of a tensor power

proof.text: The local sections in step 5 belong to the sheaf of modules $N^{\otimes n}$, with the underlying abelian sheaf of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Since $(V_i)$ covers $Z$, the gluing and uniqueness axioms in [def-sc-zariski-site] give exactly one global section $t$ with these restrictions. This applies to every $n\geq1$ and $s$, with the same $N,f_i$ of step 3. An empty cover can only cover the empty scheme; the same empty-cover sheaf axiom gives its unique section.
